purpose: Icosapent ethyl is used to lower very high levels of triglycerides (a type of fat) in your blood. It is also used in adults who already have heart disease or diabetes with other risk factors to help reduce the chance of having a heart attack, stroke, or other serious heart problems. Your doctor may prescribe it along with a statin (cholesterol-lowering) medication and a healthy diet.
how_it_works: Icosapent ethyl is a highly purified form of a fish oil called EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid). It works by reducing the amount of triglycerides your liver makes and helping your body clear them from your blood more efficiently. Think of it as helping to clean up the extra fat in your bloodstream that could otherwise clog your arteries over time.
common_side_effects: Muscle and joint pain, swelling in the hands or feet, constipation, gout flare-ups, irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation), and a fishy taste or burping. Most side effects are mild and manageable.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fish or shellfish before taking this medication. It may increase your risk of atrial fibrillation (an irregular heartbeat), especially if you already have a heart rhythm problem. It can also slightly increase the risk of bleeding, so let your doctor know if you take blood thinners like warfarin. Do not take more than prescribed, and always take it with food.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 2 capsules (2 grams) taken twice a day with food, for a total of 4 grams per day. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
